title: The stranger in white
hook: Jibril, unknown, asks about Islam, iman, ihsan and the Hour
carry: he came to teach you your religion
tomorrow: if Islam is a building, what's holding it up?

segments.voice: Yesterday: actions are by intentions. One road, two journeys, and the difference never showed. What did I intend? Today, a man nobody knows walks into the circle.
screen: `WHAT DID I INTEND?` → `A MAN NOBODY KNOWS.`

segments.voice: A good teacher sometimes asks a question she already knows the answer to. So, what's seven times eight? Not to find out. To get it said out loud, in front of everyone. Keep that in your pocket. Umar, yesterday's narrator, describes a day sitting with the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, when a man walks in. His clothes are extremely white, his hair extremely black. There's no sign of travel on him, and none of them knows who he is. Two things that can't both be true: he's come from somewhere, and he's come from nowhere. He sits down close, knee to knee with the Prophet, and starts asking.
screen: `WHAT'S SEVEN TIMES EIGHT?` → `WHITE CLOTHES, NO DUST.` → `NOBODY KNOWS HIM.`

segments.voice: What is Islam? To testify there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger, to pray, to give zakat, to fast Ramadan, and to make the pilgrimage if you're able. What is iman, faith? To believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its bad. What is ihsan, excellence? To worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. And the Hour, when is it? The one asked knows no more about it than the one asking. Now the strange part. After the answers, the stranger says: you've spoken truly. Umar says they were amazed: he asks, and then he confirms. Who does that? Someone who already knows. The man leaves. A while later the Prophet asks Umar if he knows who the questioner was, and then tells him: it was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion. So the questions were never for the asker. They were for the people sitting in the circle, who heard the whole religion laid out in three rings: what you do, what you believe, and how you stand before Allah while you do it. An angel teaching by quiz.
screen: `ISLAM, IMAN, IHSAN, THE HOUR.` · `HE ASKS, THEN SAYS: TRUE.` · `IT WAS JIBRIL.` · `THREE RINGS: DO, BELIEVE, STAND.` · then, large: `HE CAME TO TEACH YOU YOUR RELIGION.`

segments.voice: Sit the way a student sits close to a teacher: upright, knees settled, hands resting on your thighs. Go back through the three answers slowly in your mind, one at a time: what you do, what you believe, and worship as though you see Him. Stay with that last one, and the line after it, for the rest of the sit.
The stranger in white: Jibril, the angel Gabriel, who came as a questioner. His questions became the three words of the hadith: Islam, iman, ihsan.
Pocket this one: he came to teach you your religion, by asking and not by lecturing. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1430 COUNTS.` → `YEAR FIVE · 4 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: IF ISLAM IS A BUILDING, WHAT'S HOLDING IT UP?`

howItsDone: Teachers use the hadith of Jibril as an outline of the faith in three parts, Islam, iman and ihsan, and students learn its questions and answers, often in Arabic as well.

fork.setup: your little cousin is learning the steps of prayer, and you're fairly sure she knows them. how do you help them stick?
options: ask her to walk you through them, and tell her each time she's right.
recite all the steps for her again, slowly, so nothing gets missed.
skip it: if she already knows them, there's nothing left to teach.
fork.reveal: Jibril taught by asking and confirming: 'you've spoken truly.' the questions put the answers out loud, where everyone could hear them.

original.note: Arabic: Gabriel, the angel. in this hadith he arrives as an unknown questioner.

trapdoor: what you thought: a mysterious visitor story.

what a scholar hears: 'you have spoken truly' from the questioner, and the line that the one asked about the Hour knows no more than the one asking.

chat.says: ok intention set ✅ co-teacher says 'don't lecture, ask.' but asking stuff i already know feels fake??
options: Not fake. Asking what you know gets it said out loud. Jibril taught that way.
A bit fake. Real teachers explain; questions only count when you don't know.
Ask only what you can't answer yourself, so it's honest for everyone there.
chat.meaning: Jibril asked questions he knew the answers to and confirmed each one, so the people listening would learn their religion.

iman.meaning: faith: believing in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, the decree

ihsan.meaning: excellence: worship as though you see Allah

zakat.meaning: the yearly giving owed from wealth

Ramadan.meaning: the month Muslims fast from dawn to sunset

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 8 (Umar: the stranger in white; Islam, iman, ihsan, the Hour; 'it was Jibril')

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 (recipe v3): puzzle shape; the odd detail is a questioner who confirms the answers ('you have spoken truly'), which Umar says amazed them. Confirm the paraphrase of Sahih Muslim 8, including 'a while later' (Umar says he stayed a while before the Prophet asked him).
The signs of the Hour (the slave woman giving birth to her mistress; barefoot herdsmen competing in tall buildings) are left out for length.
Practice: the hadith says he placed his hands on his thighs; whose thighs is read differently by commentators, so the practice only borrows 'sitting like a student' and doesn't attribute the posture.
Gloss 'zakat: the yearly giving owed from wealth' and 'Ramadan: fast from dawn to sunset' are general definitions; confirm wording.
Amira storyline: after setting her intention (1429), her co-teacher tells her 'don't lecture, ask'. Dadi Fatima's next appearance is planned for 1435.
2026-10-07 (job 3): new recipe data added (chat, gloss, recall); confirm the chat reply, glosses, scripts and pronunciations with the Keeper.
